dedupe_keys.name: hierarchical compromise optimisation of ambulance locations under stochastic travel times two stage stochastic model and bfc csc algorithm

description: This software decides where to station ambulances when travel times are uncertain, balancing several goals in order of priority. The producers are Imanol Gago-Carro of the Basque Center for Applied Mathematics, Unai Aldasoro and María Merino of the University of the Basque Country, and Dae-Jin Lee of IE University, who published the method in Computers and Operations Research in 2025. It is a two-stage stochastic integer programme: ambulance bases are chosen first, then performance is evaluated over many travel time scenarios, and a hierarchical compromise approach with a dedicated algorithm (BFC-CSC) trades off objectives such as coverage and response time. Coverage in the study was the Basque public emergency medical service in Spain, but under a confidentiality agreement the repository contains only a small example instance. The Python scripts, example data and output logs are available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence; a companion record for a distributionally robust version had no files attached. Caveats: needs the commercial CPLEX solver, real data are not released, and documentation is limited to the folder structure and paper. Simulation uses: planning ambulance bases that stay effective when congestion or road disruption make travel times unpredictable. Related records: the Fez-Meknes ambulance data (data-fez-meknes-ambulance-deployment) offer a public test instance, and OpenEMS (model-openems-ambulance-deployment) simulates deployment.
